name: Round Marriage
description: It's marriage season in Ringland! Ringland has a form of a circle's boundary of length $$$L$$$. There are $$$n$$$ bridegrooms and $$$n$$$ brides, and bridegrooms decided to marry brides. Of course, each bridegroom should choose exactly one bride, and each bride should be chosen by exactly one bridegroom. All objects in Ringland are located on the boundary of the circle, including the capital, bridegrooms' castles and brides' palaces. The castle of the $$$i$$$-th bridegroom is located at the distance $$$a_i$$$ from the capital in clockwise direction, and the palace of the $$$i$$$-th bride is located at the distance $$$b_i$$$ from the capital in clockwise direction. Let's define the inconvenience of a marriage the maximum distance that some bride should walk along the circle from her palace to her bridegroom's castle in the shortest direction (in clockwise or counter-clockwise direction). Help the bridegrooms of Ringland to choose brides in such a way that the inconvenience of the marriage is the smallest possible.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$L$$$ ($$$1 \leq n \leq 2 \cdot 10^{5}$$$, $$$1 \leq L \leq 10^{9}$$$) — the number of bridegrooms and brides and the length of Ringland. The next line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$0 \leq a_i \lt L$$$) — the distances from the capital to the castles of bridegrooms in clockwise direction. The next line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n$$$ ($$$0 \leq b_i \lt L$$$) — the distances from the capital to the palaces of brides in clockwise direction.
output_specification: In the only line print the smallest possible inconvenience of the wedding, where the inconvenience is the largest distance traveled by a bride.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 981F — Round Marriage [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
